body.head: You Can't Run Away From Yourself

div.p: I was tired of writing and sick of New York. I felt like a poor little fly caught in the cogs of its mighty machinery. An immense nostalgia took possession of me—a longing for something other than I had known. Writing became a sort of torment—somehing I had literally to dirve myself to. Many a time I have laid my head down among my papers and pencils and cried—hopelessly, for there seemed no escape for me. The were many dependent upon me. I suppose I was in a sort of pathological condition.
